reviewed.title: `renderToString` disposes its root via `setTimeout`; graphs are retained across synchronous renders
reviewed.body:
**Version:** 2.0.0-rc.8 (`@solidjs/web`)

`packages/web/src/server.ts` ~1534:

```ts
let html = root(
  d => {
    setTimeout(d);
    return resolveSSRSync(escape(code()));
  },
  { id: renderId }
);
```

The root (and every memo/computation created under it) lives until the next macrotask. In any code path that renders more than once per task — benchmarks, batch pre-rendering, tests, `Promise.all` over many `renderToString` calls — nothing is released until the loop yields.

## Measured

Rendering `@yak/solid`'s base runtime (one memo per element) 1000 elements per call, tight loop, `--expose-gc`:

| renders | heap growth |
|---:|---:|
| 500 | +121 MB |
| 2500 | +608 MB |

≈243 KB retained per render; the same loop with a `setImmediate` yield between renders stays flat. React's `renderToString` is flat in the tight loop. The practical effect: a synchronous `renderToString` microbenchmark understated that runtime by 2–6× on larger workloads purely from GC pressure ([ryansolid/yak-bench](https://github.com/ryansolid/yak-bench), see the method notes), and the published Solid-vs-React numbers in [next-yak#644](https://github.com/DigitecGalaxus/next-yak/pull/644) were taken with exactly such a loop.

Even on a real server this holds each request's whole reactive graph one macrotask longer than necessary.

## Why it's deferred (to confirm)

Presumably so that cleanups (head-tag registrations, `httpStatus`/`httpHeader` scope declarations, asset tracking) don't run before `serializeFragmentAssets` / `renderShellHead` / `assembleDocument` read their state — the streaming path documents "the head is committed right before the render's final dispose".

## Proposed fix

Capture `d` and call it synchronously at the end of `renderToString`, after `assembleDocument` — same ordering guarantee, no macrotask hold. If something genuinely needs the dispose to happen after the caller receives the string, `queueMicrotask` bounds the retention to the current task instead of the next turn of the event loop.

## Notes

- `renderToStream` has its own dispose plumbing (`if (firstFlushed) dispose()`); check whether the sync path can share it.
- A regression test: render N times in a loop, force GC, assert heap is bounded (or assert `getOwner()`-visible disposal via an `onCleanup` counter that must equal N before the loop returns).

reviewed.body: ### Describe the bug In Solid 2.0.0-beta.17 streaming SSR, a nested `` whose children have no pending async work can permanently deadlock an enclosing ``. The real TanStack Start repro is a billing-overview page. Its outer reveal group contains a monthly-statement `` slot, which resolves after about 1.2 seconds, and a reusable Account sidebar. The sidebar always wraps its children in `` so it can coordinate async cards on other pages; on this page it contains only static content. The nested group registers itself as a composite slot of the outer group. Since none of its children register a streamed fragment, it reports full resolution to its parent but never reports minimal resolution. reviewed.title: 2.0.0-beta.21 | `affects` should have higher priority over uninitialized state of a store. when checking for pending
reviewed.body:
### Describe the bug



### **Summary**
`isPending(store.a)` throws a `NotReady` error when the store is still in its uninitialized state, even if `affects(store, "a")` has already marked the key as pending. This makes `isPending` behave as a **three‑state check** (`true | false | throws`) instead of a simple boolean, and prevents using `isPending` as a safe affordance before the store path is initialized.

### **Current Behavior**
- When `store.a` has not yet been initialized, calling `isPending(store.a)` throws a `NotReady` error.
- This happens **even if** `affects(store, "a")` was called beforehand, which should explicitly mark the path as pending.
- In development mode, this error is *not* thrown. Instead:
  - `isPending(store.a)` returns `true` when `affects(store, "a")` was called.
  - It returns `false` when no pending marker exists.
  - This suggests the logic already supports a boolean interpretation, but the production error‑throwing overrides it.

### **Problem**
This behavior makes `isPending` effectively a **three‑state API**:

1. `true` — pending  
2. `false` — not pending  
3. `throws` — store not initialized  

Because of the thrown error, `isPending` cannot be used safely as a simple affordance in UI code until the store path has been initialized. This creates race conditions where the same code sometimes works and sometimes throws depending on initialization timing.

### **Why This Is an Issue**
- The uninitialized state takes precedence over the explicit pending marker, which is unintuitive.
- It forces developers to add loading boundaries or initialization guards even when they only want to check pending state.
- It creates surprising differences between dev and production behavior.
- It makes `isPending` unsuitable as a drop‑in `isLoading`‑style check, because it can unexpectedly throw.

### **Expected Behavior**
`isPending` should behave as a **pure boolean check**, even when the store path is uninitialized:

- If `affects(store, "a")` was called → `isPending(store.a)` should return `true`.
- If no pending marker exists → `isPending(store.a)` should return `false`.
- The uninitialized state should **not** cause `isPending` to throw.

If a separate mechanism is needed to detect whether a read would trigger a loading boundary, that should be exposed as a dedicated API (e.g., `isLoading(store.a)`), rather than overloading `isPending` with error‑throwing semantics.

### **Example**
```jsx
<>
  {isPending(() => store.a) ? "Pending" : "Not Pending"}
</>
```

This currently throws in production if `store.a` is uninitialized, even when the developer explicitly marked it as pending.

### **Conclusion**
Unless there is a specific design reason for `isPending` to participate in `NotReady` error throwing (and I cannot identify one), it seems more consistent and ergonomic for `isPending` to remain a boolean check and not throw for uninitialized store paths—especially when an explicit `affects` marker exists.



 

### Your Example Website or App

.

### Steps to Reproduce the Bug or Issue

.

### Expected behavior

.

### Screenshots or Videos

_No response_

### Platform

.

### Additional context

if `isPending` will not throw, on uninitialized `store.a` will simply show 
`not pending | Hello` 
```js
<>
<Loading  fallback={"Loading..."}>
  {isPending(store.a) ? "pending" : "not pending |" }
Hello
</Loading>
</>
```

but that is expected once you understand the isPending returning `false` for non initialized pending store state. 

we will need an explicit trigger or another guard check for affordance in both cases 

`isPendingOrLoading()`


Loading boundary will not be triggered it is guarded by isPendingOrLoading
```js
<>
<Loading  fallback={"Loading..."}>
  {isPendingOrLoading(store.a) ? "pending" : "ready |" }
Hello

</Loading>
</>
```


Loading boundary will trigger but from the explicit read of an uninitialized store 

```js
<>
<Loading  fallback={"Loading..."}>
  {isPending(store.a) ? "pending" : "not pending |" }
Hello
or read {store.a} explicitly to trigger Loading boundary first for the "edge case"
</Loading>
</>
```

reviewed.title: navigate() from flight-data consumer can silently drop a relative-Location redirect (reliable with absolute URLs)
Action busy state, onSettled hooks and submissions release before the transition commits
reviewed.body:
## Summary

Three things an action does on the client happen when its generator finishes, not when its transition commits:

- the form's `aria-busy` is removed (`setFormBusy(form, -1)` in the `finally` after `settleActionResult(run(...))`);
- `action.onSettled` hooks fire;
- the submission is recorded in `useSubmissions`.

`action()` in `@solidjs/signals` resolves its promise in `done()` — it removes the iterator, schedules a flush, and resolves immediately — so everything chained on that promise runs before the commit. When nothing holds the transition, release and commit land in back-to-back microtasks and it looks right. When something does, it doesn't.

Separately, `aria-busy` is stripped by any server-component morph of the form (server HTML never carries it), and nothing reapplies it while the submission is still in flight.

## Where it shows

The invariant we want: **a form is busy from submit until the commit that makes its outcome visible, whatever that commit was merged with.**

| case | today |
| --- | --- |
| independent action, transition not held | correct by timing luck (adjacent microtasks) |
| transition held by async (e.g. the refetch after a response without single-flight data) | mark clears while the old markup still shows; the update pops in later |
| transition merged through shared optimistic writes | mark clears while the prediction still shows |
| action merged with a pending navigation | releases before the navigation commits |
| another response's morph touches the form | `aria-busy` stripped mid-flight, not reapplied |

The same timing affects `onSettled` users: todos-server clears the add input in `addTodo.onSettled`, which can run before the new row appears.

## Constraints on a fix

- **No shared reactive state for busy.** A router-level optimistic store (`inflight[url] = true`, auto-reverting) is tempting, but it is a shared optimistic write — it would entangle overlapping submissions that otherwise land independently. An indicator must never change when results land.
- **Key by the form's `action` URL, not the element.** `.with()` makes the URL unique per row. A `WeakMap<HTMLFormElement, number>` loses the mark when a morph replaces the node, and misses programmatic calls of the same request (e.g. `submission.retry()` shows no mark today).
- **Reapply on re-claim.** The frames runtime already re-claims `form[action]` after a morph changes its attributes; a claim handler that reads the busy record restores the attribute.

## Candidate

Release from a commit callback rather than the promise. An unowned `onSettled` enqueues onto the global queue; registered from the action's final slice while its transition is active, it should fire when that transition commits — merged or not — and, being an effect rather than a write, cannot entangle anything. Then:

- busy: a non-reactive `Map<string, number>` keyed by URL, incremented on submit, decremented in that callback, projected onto `form[action="<url>"]` and reapplied by the claim handler;
- `onSettled` hooks and the submission record move to the same callback.

**To verify first** (signals-level test): an `onSettled` registered in an action's final slice fires only when the transition commits — when held by a pending async read, and when merged with a second action.

**Open decision:** whether core `action()` should resolve its promise at commit instead (making `await action()` mean "it's on screen"). That changes documented behaviour of a core public API, so it's a framework decision, not a router detail.

## Context

Found while rebuilding the todos-server example ([solidjs/solid#3717](https://github.com/solidjs/solid/pull/3717)) around router-driven intent (`aria-busy` + `:has()` CSS). An earlier attempt that only reapplied `aria-busy` on re-claim was dropped from the claims fix in favour of fixing the release point properly.

reviewed.title: Client bundle statically imports @solidjs/web/server-functions/server (decodeFlashCookie): server entry and a second signals copy load in Vite dev
reviewed.body:
**Version:** `@solidjs/router@2.0.0-next.28` (also next.13), `@solidjs/web@2.0.0-rc.x`, Vite dev with `@solidjs/vite-plugin`.

## What happens

`dist/index.js` and `dist/data/action.js` statically import the runtime's **server** entry from a module that is also shipped to the browser:

```js
// dist/index.js:4, dist/data/action.js:6
import { decodeFlashCookie } from '@solidjs/web/server-functions/server';
```

The only call site is guarded (`installRouterIntegrations`: `if (isServer) provideFlashDecoder(decodeFlashCookie)`), and the comment says client builds tree-shake the codec away. That holds for a production bundle (`@solidjs/web` is `sideEffects: false`, `isServer` folds). It does not hold in **Vite dev**, where nothing is tree-shaken: the browser loads the router, follows the static import, and pulls in the server-functions server entry and everything under it.

Observed in a browser (resource timing, `pnpm dev` of an SSR app):

```
/node_modules/.vite/deps/@solidjs_web_server-functions.js
/@fs/.../packages/web/server-functions/dist/server.dev.js     ← server entry, in the browser
/@fs/.../packages/solid/dist/internal.js                       ← via `reportServerError` from solid-js/internal
/@fs/.../packages/signals/dist/dev.js                          ← a second copy of the reactive engine
/@fs/.../packages/signals/dist/dev-shared.js
```

In a linked workspace (pnpm `workspace:`/`link:`) those `@fs` modules are not the pre-bundled `.vite/deps` copies, so the page runs **two instances of `@solidjs/signals`** — one from the optimized `solid-js` chunk, one raw through `solid-js/internal`. In a regular install the optimizer will probably fold them into one graph, but the server-only codec (WebCrypto cookie decryption, `AsyncLocalStorage` request context, the `/server` export's whole surface) is still delivered to every dev page.

## Why it matters

- Dev-only weight and load time for every router user, on every page.
- With linked packages (which is how the runtime itself and the templates are developed), a duplicate engine instance — a class of bug that is very hard to attribute when it shows up (`instanceof`/context/symbol mismatches, owners from two schedulers).
- The pattern is fragile: it depends on a bundler proving `isServer` false and on `sideEffects: false` staying true for `@solidjs/web`.

## Suggestion

Keep the decoder off the client module graph entirely rather than relying on elimination:

- install it from the router's own server entry (`dist/server.js` already exists and is server-only), e.g. `configureServerFunctionsServer`/SSR setup calls `provideFlashDecoder(decodeFlashCookie)`; or
- `await import('@solidjs/web/server-functions/server')` inside the `isServer` branch of `installRouterIntegrations` — the branch is already async-tolerant since the codec became async in web rc.7.

Happy to send a PR for whichever shape you prefer.

## Repro

Any SSR app with `pnpm dev`; open the network panel filtered to `server-functions` / `internal` — the server entry loads on the client. With `@solidjs/web` linked from a checkout, `signals/dist/dev.js` appears alongside the optimized deps chunk.

conclusion: No matching resource-less performance-track expiry report
